And these estimates do not account for the many people with undiagnosed COPD or those in earlier stages of the disorder. item.description: Joanne Liu was International President of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) from 2013 until 2019. item.title: [The Lancet] [Perspectives] Horology and the heart
item.description: At the turn of the 17th century, the Venetian physician Santorio Santorio (1561–1636) described an instrument that rendered the pulse measurable. A weight was hung from a cord against a graduated scale and set swinging, the cord lengthened or shortened until the swing matched the beat beneath the doctor's fingers; a reading could then be taken from the scale. Santorio named it the pulsilogium, one of the first instruments of precision in medicine. Until then the pulse had been read by touch. item.title: [The Lancet] [Correspondence] Indonesia's fires are a health emergency
item.description: Since July, 2026, fires have burned across Kalimantan, Sumatra, and Papua. By Sept 9, Indonesia's Ministry of Health estimated that smoke had affected 12·5 million people;1 by Nov 2, facilities in seven provinces had recorded 401 586 acute respiratory infections, of which 91 913 were in children aged 5 years or younger.2 The smoke has crossed borders: on Oct 14, Singapore recorded a 1-h PM2·5 concentration of 284 μg/m3, its highest in 2026, while haze caused school closures in several Malaysian states and suspended face-to-face schooling nationwide in Timor-Leste for 3 days.

item.title: [The Lancet] [Correspondence] The PSMAddition trial in metastatic prostate cancer
item.description: We read with great interest the report of the phase 3 PSMAddition trial by Scott T Tagawa and colleagues,1 which evaluated [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 added to androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) in prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The investigators should be congratulated for completing a large and methodologically rigorous radioligand trial. The improvement in radiographic progression-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0·72; 95% CI 0·58–0·90) is clinically relevant.

item.title: [The Lancet] [Correspondence] The PSMAddition trial in metastatic prostate cancer – Authors’ reply

item.description: Gransee and colleagues1 reported a demanding trial with an unusually practical protocol: diaphragm shear wave elastography across graded inspiratory loading, completed preoperatively in under 30 min without disrupting anaesthetic workflow. Among their secondary findings, the authors describe a negative association between the pre-fentanyl Young’s modulus range (E range) and the fentanyl-induced change in that range (ΔE range; P<0.001; r2=0.184; their Fig. 3b), advanced in the Discussion as the basis of a candidate biomarker of opioid susceptibility.

item.title: [British Journal of Anaesthesia] Inflammasome–caspase-1 activation is associated with infections in systemic inflammatory response syndrome after cardiac surgery: a prospective translational study
item.description: Cardiac surgery triggers the systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), characterised by a dysregulated immune response involving concurrent pro- and anti-inflammatory activation. Postoperative immunosuppression increases susceptibility to postoperative infections, prolonged hospitalisation, and mortality. After burns and stroke, circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) initiates immune dysregulation via inflammasome activation. Whether this mechanism similarly contributes to SIRS-associated immunosuppression after cardiac surgery is unknown.
